title: Kent village once named England's most haunted is train ride from south east London
excerpt: A Kent village once recognised as England's most haunted is offering visitors a spooky autumn day out just over an hour from south east London.
content:
A Kent village once recognised as England's most haunted is offering visitors a spooky autumn day out just over an hour from south east London.

Pluckley, near Ashford, has long been associated with ghost stories and paranormal legends, helping it earn a place in the Guinness World Records as the "most haunted village in England" in 1989.

The picturesque village can be reached by train from London Charing Cross or by car from south east London for anyone looking for a car-free day trip this autumn.

While Pluckley's ghostly reputation continues to attract curious visitors, the village is also known for its historic buildings, countryside walks and connections to television.

Dering Wood, Pluckley (Image: Tim Sheerman-Chase/Flickr)

According to local legend, a number of spirits are said to roam the area.

Among the most famous tales is that of the Highwayman of Fright Corner, who is said to appear near the Pinnock after reportedly being killed in an ambush centuries ago.

Another story centres around the Lady of Rose Court, a tragic figure believed to wander the village after taking her own life following a failed romance.

One of Pluckley's best-known locations is the Screaming Woods at Dering, where eerie cries and unexplained sounds have reportedly been heard after dark.

Other local legends include sightings of a phantom coach travelling through the village lanes, a ghostly schoolmaster in Dicky Buss's Lane and a mysterious white dog near St Nicholas' Church.

The village's reputation for hauntings extends to some of its pubs too. The Black Horse Inn, a 15th-century coaching inn, has become closely associated with local ghost stories over the years, while The Dering Arms is said to be haunted by the spirit of a Victorian-era woman.

Black Horse pub, Pluckley (Image: Bob Donkin/Flickr)

Set within the rolling Wealden countryside, the village is surrounded by scenic walking routes that make it particularly attractive during the autumn months.

One popular option is the Greensand Way, a long-distance path which passes through Pluckley before continuing towards Ashford.

The route takes walkers through fields, woodland and historic landscapes, including the grounds surrounding Godinton Park.

Those looking for something shorter can follow the Pluckley Circular Walk, a route associated with author H.E. Bates that offers a gentler way to explore the surrounding countryside.

The village also holds a place in television history after featuring in ITV's adaptation of The Darling Buds of May.

Whether drawn by the ghost stories, the autumn scenery or its traditional village charm, Pluckley remains one of Kent's most intriguing destinations for a seasonal day trip.
